Bernie Sanders wants to raise the wages of H1B workers

The title is a bit misleading. Sanders argues that raising wages of H1B workers will actually discourage businesses from hiring foreign workers. Though this makes sense, the law also states that businesses can only hire foreign workers after they have attempted to find a qualified American worker first. If the company is unable to fill the position with a qualified American, then it may seek workers from outside the U.S.

Disney attempted to do this earlier this year thinking they could save money by paying these workers less than their American counterparts. After Disney implemented mass layoffs, specifically in their tech area, there was an uproar. It seems that Disney misunderstood the law and was forced to rescind the layoffs.

In the free enterprise system, the law of supply and demand has a direct impact on prices, including wages and salaries. Someone with a rare skill is certainly in position to demand a higher salary. However, this is not what is happening with H1B workers. Corporations have been exploiting foreigner workers desire to live and work in the U.S., which has allowed these businesses to pay lower salaries. This is perhaps why Sanders is calling for higher wages. He knows that companies are desperate to pay employees as little as possible.
